angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 413,942 km at 76.96 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.9931 +/- 0.0228 mas (same row, RUWE 1.47): 76.96 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.595 +/- 0.031 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-321 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 413,942 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.578 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-321 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3750 +/- 510 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-321 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-321 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-321.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.651, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, K2-321: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-321 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.148 dex, from Thygesen et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-321 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.20066, from Thygesen et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 3856449627544923392, flags_flame 00: age_flame 10.874001 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 6.185155 to 13.5)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
